blocks.text: The petrol in a keke napep, the kerosene in a lantern, the gas in a cooking cylinder and the bitumen on the expressway all came out of the same barrel of Nigerian crude. They differ only in how many carbon atoms are chained together, and all of them are alkanes.

blocks.title: Alkanes
blocks.text: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2. Saturated means every carbon-to-carbon bond is a single bond, so the molecule holds the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms. They form a homologous series, meaning consecutive members differ by a CH2 unit.

blocks.caption: The first ten alkanes; boiling point rises with molecular size

blocks.markdown:
## Features of a homologous series

- All members share one general formula
- Consecutive members differ by CH2, a mass difference of 14
- All members have similar chemical properties, because they share the same kind of bonding
- Physical properties change gradually with increasing chain length: boiling point, melting point, density and viscosity all rise, while volatility and flammability fall
- All members can be prepared by similar methods

The rise in boiling point happens because larger molecules have more electrons, so the van der Waals forces between them are stronger and more energy is needed to separate them.

## Isomerism

**Structural isomers** are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae. Butane, C4H10, has two:

- **Butane**, a straight chain: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3
- **2-methylpropane**, a branched chain: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3

Branching lowers the boiling point, because a branched molecule is more compact and its surface makes less contact with neighbours, weakening the van der Waals forces. Pentane, C5H12, has three isomers, and hexane has five.

blocks.title: Naming a branched alkane by IUPAC rules

steps.text: Find the longest continuous carbon chain. Reading through the CH3, CH, CH2 and CH3 in line gives four carbons, so the parent alkane is butane.
Identify the substituent groups attached to that chain. There is one CH3 branch, which is a methyl group.
Number the chain from the end that gives the substituent the lower number. From the left the methyl is on carbon 2; from the right it would be on carbon 3, so number from the left.
Combine the position, the substituent name and the parent name, separating numbers from words with a hyphen.
The name is 2-methylbutane. Check the formula: C4H10 in the chain plus CH3 as the branch gives C5H12, which fits CnH2n+2 with n = 5.

blocks.markdown:
## Reactions of alkanes

Alkanes are relatively unreactive because the C-C and C-H bonds are strong and non-polar. They have two important reactions.

**1. Combustion**

Complete combustion in plenty of air gives carbon dioxide and water:

CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O

Incomplete combustion in a limited supply of air gives poisonous carbon monoxide or soot:

2CH4 + 3O2 -> 2CO + 4H2O

**2. Substitution with halogens**

In the presence of ultraviolet light or bright sunlight, a hydrogen atom is replaced one at a time by a halogen atom:

CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl

The reaction continues to CH2Cl2, CHCl3 and finally CCl4 if excess chlorine is present. In the dark there is no reaction at all.

blocks.title: Why generators kill
blocks.text: Running a petrol generator in an enclosed room causes incomplete combustion because oxygen is limited. The carbon monoxide produced is colourless and odourless, and it binds to haemoglobin far more strongly than oxygen does. This is the chemistry behind a tragedy reported in Nigerian newspapers every year.

blocks.title: Substitution, not addition
blocks.text: Alkanes are saturated, so they cannot undergo addition reactions. If a question mentions an alkane reacting with chlorine, the answer is substitution and it requires ultraviolet light. Reserve addition for alkenes and alkynes.

points: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CnH2n+2.
Members of a homologous series differ by CH2 and show a gradual change in physical properties.
Boiling point rises with chain length because van der Waals forces increase.
Structural isomers share a molecular formula but differ in the arrangement of atoms, and branching lowers the boiling point.
Complete combustion gives carbon dioxide and water; incomplete combustion gives carbon monoxide or soot.
Alkanes undergo substitution with halogens in ultraviolet light, never addition.
